name: Dich Long Pagoda and Cave
kicker: Cave pagoda where the wind flutes
summary: Climb 105 stone steps to a cave pagoda 15 km north of the city, where wind at the mouth sounds like a flute. The plan places it in xã Gia Thanh, about 600 m west of the Đoan Vĩ bridge and about 80 km south of Hanoi. The national ranking is 1990. The ticket board does not list a fee.
dotReason: A cave pagoda north of the valley, one stop
getThere: About 15 km north of the city, xã Gia Thanh, huyện Gia Viễn.
heroCaption: The yellow pagoda against the cliff at Dich Long
body: The name means the sound of a flute. The tourism plan says that when you stand at the cave mouth the wind comes through like that. It places the pagoda on the north side of xã Gia Thanh, about 600 m west of the Đoan Vĩ bridge, about 15 km north of the city, and about 80 km south of Hanoi. Other names on that page are chùa Hang, Cổ Am Tự, and Nham Sơn. The 2017 tourism page says Minh Mạng granted the title Nam thiên đệ tam động.

The plan describes a pagoda and a communal hall on a court of more than 7,000 square metres. The outer stone hall, called đình Đá, is dated Bảo Đại 11 (1936), with 12 stone columns carved with dragons. From the court you pass a side shrine, then more than ten steps to the shrine of Đức Ông, then 105 stone steps to the cave. The cave door carries six characters: Nham Sơn động and Cổ Am tự. A large bell is dated Minh Mệnh 8 (1827). The 2017 page says the Ministry of Culture and Information ranked it a national historic and cultural relic in 1990.
The festival on the plan is the 6th and 7th of lunar month 3. The communal hall is for Nguyễn Minh Không. A gate fee and a daily hour were not on the tourism page or the ticket board.

gettingThere: Ride north from the city. The tourism plan prints about 15 km, and about 600 m west of the Đoan Vĩ bridge once you are on the north side of xã Gia Thanh. It also prints about 80 km south of Hanoi. Minutes were not printed.

legs.heading: From the city
legs.body: About 15 km north, then about 600 m west of the Đoan Vĩ bridge. Both figures are on the provincial tourism plan. Minutes were not printed.

legs.heading: From Hanoi
legs.body: About 80 km south on the same plan. A drive time was not printed.

closed: No weekly closing day was printed. Check on arrival.
admissionNote: A fee was not on the 2017 tourism page, the tourism plan, or the Tràng An ticket board opened 23 October 2026.
